cards.b: A design in which instructions and data are stored in the same main memory (RAM) and fetched by the CPU one after another.
Arithmetic logic unit: does calculations and logic operations such as AND, OR, NOT and comparisons.
Decodes instructions, sends control signals and controls the flow of data around the CPU.
PC: address of the next instruction to fetch. MAR: address of the memory location being read from or written to.
MDR: data or instruction just fetched. CIR: instruction being decoded and executed. ACC: results of ALU calculations.

cards.f: Address bus, data bus, control bus
cards.b: Address bus carries addresses (one way, CPU to memory). Data bus carries data and instructions (both ways). Control bus carries control signals.
PC copied to MAR; PC incremented; instruction at that address copied from RAM to MDR; then MDR to CIR.
Control unit decodes the instruction in the CIR using the instruction set. Then the instruction is carried out, e.g. ALU calculates or PC changes on a jump.
Number of fetch–decode–execute cycles per second, in Hz. Higher is faster but produces more heat.
Each core runs its own FDE cycle, so more instructions run at once. It only helps if software can use several cores.
Small, very fast memory in or next to the CPU that stores frequently used data and instructions.
A computer system built into a device to do one dedicated task, e.g. washing machine, alarm, traffic lights.
An input device that measures a physical property such as temperature and sends readings to a processor.
An output device that moves or controls something when it gets a signal from the processor, e.g. motor, valve, heater.
Laser draws the page on a charged drum; toner sticks to it, is transferred to paper and fused by heat.

gaps.s: The ___ register stores the address of the next instruction to be fetched.
The ___ register holds the results of calculations made by the ALU.
The ___ bus carries memory addresses from the CPU to memory.
The list of all the commands a CPU can carry out is its ___ set.
A ___ is a processing unit inside the CPU that can run its own fetch–decode–execute cycle.
A 3D printer builds an object ___ by layer.
In a sensor-based system, the processor sends a signal to an ___ to make something happen.

short.q: Describe the purpose of the MAR and the MDR.
short.model: The MAR holds the address of the memory location that is to be read from or written to. The MDR holds the data or instruction that has just been fetched from, or is about to be written to, memory.
points: MDR holds data/instruction fetched or to be written

short.q: Explain why a computer with more cores may not run a program twice as fast.
short.model: More cores allow more instructions to be processed at the same time, but only if the software can split its tasks across cores. Many programs cannot, so the speed-up is smaller.
points: more cores allow tasks run at same time
only if software can use multiple cores

short.q: A central heating system keeps a house at 21 °C. Describe how a temperature sensor is used.
short.model: The sensor sends readings to the processor continuously. The processor compares each reading with the stored value of 21 °C and, if it is too low, signals an actuator to switch the heater on (and off when too warm).
points: sensor sends readings to the processor
signal sent to an actuator / heater

short.q: Describe how a touchscreen with capacitive technology detects where it has been touched.
short.model: A finger changes the electric field on the screen. The processor calculates the position of the change in the field and treats it as the touch position.

short.q: State two features of an embedded system and give one example.
short.model: It is built into a device and does one dedicated task. Example: a washing machine controller.
points: built into a device / single dedicated task
